label: Delimiter step of long sequences whose first token is one of a/b/g/q/l/i/...
explanation: Fires almost only on the <DEL> step (92% of activation mass, 89% of active steps), when the model is about to output the first original token. It never fires in the copy phase or before t=4. Its rate rises steeply with L: about 0 for L=3-4, 11% of delimiter steps overall, 14% for L=9. It also depends on the first token (the token to be recalled): a and b are the strongest (about 6x lift), then g, q, l, i, then v, m, j, e, y, h, with a graded tail. The other 8% of mass is in the original phase, on the last one or two inputs of long sequences (orig_idx 7-8). Magnitude is largest for L=8-9 with first token a or b. The predicate (delimiter, L>=7, first token in that 12-letter set) gets dev F1 of about 0.50 with mass recall 0.75. Plenty of matching delimiter steps stay inactive, so some other unidentified factor in the sequence content gates it. It is a graded, distributed code rather than a crisp detector.
